did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with full, personal thanksgiving: “I will give you thanks with all my heart.” The psalmist is not content with inward gratitude; he also sings and openly praises the LORD.

Did you know? The psalmist combines three expressions of worship: bowing down, giving thanks, and singing. He thanks the LORD for His “steadfast love” and “faithfulness,” emphasizing His reliability and the greatness of His word.

Did you know? This verse describes a direct connection between prayer and response: the psalmist calls to the LORD, and the LORD answers him. As a result, he receives strength and inner encouragement.
Did you know? Thanksgiving to the LORD is not limited to Israel alone: the psalm describes the kings of the earth as giving thanks to the LORD after hearing the words of His mouth.

Did you know? The kings’ response is not merely an expression of thanks, but also a song about the LORD’s ways. The psalm presents the word of the LORD as leading people to recognize His greatness and praise His ways.
Did you know? This verse presents a central contrast: the LORD is exalted and majestic, yet He regards the lowly; the proud and arrogant, however, He recognizes “from afar.”

Did you know? The psalmist does not claim that believers will never face trouble. Rather, he expresses confidence that even in trouble, the LORD will preserve his life, protect him, and save him from his enemies.

Did you know? The psalm’s conclusion combines confidence and request: the psalmist believes that the LORD will fulfill His purpose for him, and at the same time asks Him not to abandon the work of His hands. This request rests on the declaration that the LORD’s steadfast love endures forever.
